sun.name: The Sun
sun.description:
The Sun is an oversized atomic engine that has been running on autopilot for **4.6 billion years** without ever stopping to refuel — *it is the fuel*. Every second, it converts the mass equivalent of **600 million cars** worth of hydrogen into pure energy; and since volumes scale as the cube, you could stack nearly **1.3 million Earths** inside it despite a diameter only 109 times larger than ours. Its outer corona is **hotter than its own surface** — a mystery that physics has still not resolved, *which has left astrophysicists collectively furious for decades*. When it sneezes — a coronal mass ejection — it hurls clouds of particles the size of several planets directly at us.

> Fortunately, we have a magnetic shield. Without it, we would resemble an overdone piece of toast.
facts: 🌌 The Sun completes one orbit around the Milky Way in roughly **225 million years** — one 'galactic year'. Since its birth, it has completed **18** of them.
🚀 The **Parker Solar Probe** is the fastest object ever built by humanity: it reaches nearly **692,000 km/h** at its closest approach to the Sun.
🔴 In about **5 billion years**, the Sun will become a red giant large enough to engulf Earth's orbit — before collapsing into a white dwarf.

mercury.name: Mercury
mercury.description:
Mercury is the planet that tried to have an atmosphere, gave it a go, and had it blown away by the Sun like a birthday candle — *it then cobbled together a replacement from gases seeping out of its own ground, which is roughly as effective as a paper raincoat*. The result: the temperature swing between day (**+430 °C**) and night (**−170 °C**) is the largest in the solar system — all on the same planet, sometimes just a few kilometres apart. Its iron core is so colossal it accounts for **57% of its total volume**, making it a shrivelling raisin that is still shrinking — Mercury has been wrinkling for billions of years, like a forgotten apple left on a windowsill. And despite its scandalous closeness to the Sun, it is **Venus** — right next door — that holds the title of hottest planet.

> Ha!
facts: 🎨 Mercury's craters are named after **artists, musicians and writers**: Beethoven, Bach, Tolstoy, Cervantes, and even Tolkien all have a crater to their name.
🧊 Despite its proximity to the Sun, Mercury has **water ice** in its polar craters, shielded by permanent shadow — never touched by a single solar ray.
🛸 The **BepiColombo** probe (ESA + JAXA), launched in 2018, is en route to Mercury and will enter orbit in **2026** — only the third mission ever sent to this planet.

venus.name: Venus
venus.description:
Venus is cosmic proof that good looks can mask a catastrophic situation — from afar, it is the brightest object in the night sky; up close, it is a **pizza oven set to maximum for 4 billion years**, draped in clouds of sulphuric acid. The atmospheric pressure equals what you would endure at **900 metres below** the ocean surface, which reduced most Soviet probes to metallic pancakes within **a few tens of minutes**, the sturdiest holding out heroically for **127 minutes** before capitulating. Venus rotates in the opposite direction to almost every other planet, *with the unsettling serenity of someone making a U-turn on the motorway*, so slowly that **one Venusian sidereal day is longer than one Venusian year**.

> On Venus, the Sun rises in the west, sets in the east, and time is a purely theoretical concept.
facts: 🔭 In **1610**, Galileo observed the **phases of Venus** through his telescope — direct proof that Venus orbits the Sun and not the Earth, helping to tip astronomy toward heliocentrism.
🌋 Venus has more than **85,000 identified volcanoes** — more than any other planet in the solar system. Some may still be active.
🗺️ Almost the entire Venusian surface was mapped by **radar** by the Magellan probe (1990–1994), since the permanent cloud cover blocks all optical observation.

earth.name: Earth
earth.description:
Earth is, to our knowledge, **the only place in the observable universe** where a living being can get up in the morning, eat a piece of buttered toast and watch the rain fall — which, on a cosmic scale, is a genuinely miraculous achievement. Liquid water on the surface, that perfectly mundane chemical curiosity here, is **absent from every other planetary surface** in the solar system; and its crust has been in perpetual motion for hundreds of millions of years, continents drifting like rafts on a semi-molten mantle, *which is either reassuring or terrifying depending on the time of day*. Seen from space, all this frantic activity vanishes entirely: our planet looks like a **small blue marble floating in absolute darkness**, sovereign and infinitely fragile.

> That contrast ought to cross our minds every time we are stuck in traffic.
facts: 🌍 Earth is the only planet in the solar system whose name **does not come from Greco-Roman mythology** — it derives from Old Germanic, related to the word for 'ground' or 'soil'.

🦕 Some **300 million years ago**, all continents were joined into a single landmass called **Pangaea** — they have been fragmenting and drifting ever since, at roughly the speed your fingernails grow.
🧲 Earth's magnetic field **reverses** roughly every 200,000 to 300,000 years: the magnetic North Pole becomes the South Pole and vice versa. The last reversal was 780,000 years ago.

moon.name: Moon
moon.description:
Our Moon was born from a cosmic industrial accident: **4.5 billion years ago**, a Mars-sized object slammed head-on into proto-Earth, hurling billions of tonnes of molten rock into space that clumped together in orbit — *it is about as elegant a birth as tumbling out of a lorry*. Since then, it has provided considerable services: it **stabilises our rotational axis** like a luxury gyroscope, preventing the seasons from becoming a chaotic nightmare, and it has gradually slowed our days down from the bare **6 hours** they lasted in the early days. In return, it drifts away from us at **3.8 cm per year** — exactly the speed at which your fingernails grow — and in a few hundred million years it will be too far away to cause total solar eclipses.

> That spectacle, unique in the solar system, will then be gone forever — and no one will have thought to back it up.
facts: 👨‍🚀 **12 humans** walked on the Moon between 1969 and 1972 — all American. Since **Apollo 17** in December 1972, no one has returned.
👣 The Apollo astronauts' footprints are **still intact** on the Moon — with no wind or rain to erase them, they could last millions of years.

🇨🇳 In **2019**, the Chinese probe **Chang'e 4** landed on the **far side** of the Moon — an absolute first: no spacecraft had ever landed there, as direct communication is impossible without a relay satellite.

mars.name: Mars
mars.description:
Mars is a planet that has **clearly seen better days**: it once had rivers, lakes, a respectable atmosphere and a protective magnetic field — then the core cooled, the magnetic field vanished, and the solar wind stripped the atmosphere away piece by piece, *like a negligent landlord dismantling a flat room by room*. What remains is spectacular scenery: a volcano whose slopes peak at **22 km**, rising above virtually all of the dense atmosphere, and a canyon so long it would **stretch across Europe from end to end**. The sky is a lovely shade of oxidised peanut butter, and dust storms can blanket **the entire planet** for months.

> Several human robots are roaming around there right now, patiently sending back their photos like conscientious tourists in a post-apocalyptic national park.
facts: 🚁 **Ingenuity** became in 2021 the **first powered aircraft to fly on another planet** — a 1.8 kg helicopter originally planned for 5 test flights, which ultimately completed **72** before coming to rest.
💥 **Phobos**, Mars's largest moon, orbits so close to the planet that it will be **torn apart by tidal forces** in about 50 million years — its debris will then form a ring around Mars.
⏱️ Due to its elliptical orbit, Mars makes a close approach to Earth every **26 months** — but at very different distances, ranging from 56 million km (favourable opposition) to 401 million km.

jupiter.name: Jupiter
jupiter.description:
Jupiter is a **gravity factory** so massive it narrowly missed a career as a star — it would only have needed to be **80 times heavier** to ignite nuclear fusion and become a pocket sun. As it stands, it settles for being **2.5 times more massive than all the other planets combined**, which is already perfectly unreasonable. Its Great Red Spot is an anticyclone **the size of the entire Earth**, active for at least **350 years**, with winds exceeding **600 km/h** — the equivalent of a category 5 hurricane that stubbornly refuses to retire. Jupiter spins so fast on its axis (**under 10 hours** per day) that its equator visibly bulges, giving it the silhouette of a flattened tangerine.

> It has at least **95 known moons**, including four discovered by Galileo in 1610 — which caused him considerable trouble with the Church.
facts: 🌊 **Europa**, a moon of Jupiter, hides beneath its ice crust an ocean of liquid water potentially containing **2 to 3 times more water** than all of Earth's oceans combined — a serious candidate for extraterrestrial life.
🌋 **Io**, another moon of Jupiter, is the most **volcanically active** body in the solar system — its permanent eruptions hurl material hundreds of kilometres into the sky.
🛡️ Thanks to its enormous mass, Jupiter acts as a **gravitational shield** for the inner planets: it deflects or captures many comets and asteroids that might otherwise strike Earth.

saturn.name: Saturn
saturn.description:
Saturn is **the great dandy of the solar system**: it wears its rings with such elegance that it has become the icon of popular astronomy — ever since Galileo, in 1610, thought he saw a planet flanked by **two large ears** when pointing his telescope at it. Those rings span **hundreds of thousands of kilometres** in diameter yet are sometimes barely thicker than a ten-storey building, *like a sheet of paper scaled up to a football stadium*. Saturn is also so low in density that it would **float on water** if a large enough ocean could be found — and according to certain theoretical models, the pressure at its core would turn carbon into **diamonds** that then fall toward the centre like hailstones, *a hypothesis so poetic that scientists secretly hope it turns out to be true*.

> Its moon Titan has lakes and rivers that are entirely real — but filled with liquid methane. Fishing there is locally inadvisable.
facts: 🛸 In **2005**, the **Huygens** probe landed on **Titan** — the only landing ever achieved in the outer solar system, 1.4 billion kilometres from the Sun. It transmitted images for 72 minutes.
💦 **Enceladus**, a moon barely 500 km across, shoots **jets of salty water** into space from a subsurface ocean — one of the most promising environments for life in the entire solar system.

⬡ Saturn's **north pole** is swept by a permanent hexagonal storm roughly **30,000 km** across — about 2.5 times the width of Earth. It has been spinning with clockwork regularity since at least 1980.

uranus.name: Uranus
uranus.description:
Uranus is the planet that decided to **lie on its side** following a titanic collision in its youth — and simply never got back up, ending up tilted at **nearly 98°** on its orbit, rolling around the Sun like a marble bowled on its side. The direct consequence: each pole spends **42 years** in full sunlight, then **42 years** in complete darkness, *which gives the concept of 'season' a somewhat discouraging existential dimension*. Its rings, discovered **by accident in 1977** when they blocked a star being observed, are so dark they reflect barely 2% of light — ghost rings, discreet to the point of invisibility. Its moons bear names drawn from **Shakespeare and Alexander Pope**, making it the only corner of the solar system with a coherent literary programme.

> Why does Uranus emit so little internal heat compared to the other giants? Scientists shrug — *with a smile that says a great deal*.
facts: 🔭 Uranus was the **first planet discovered with a telescope**, by William Herschel on **13 March 1781** — its existence was entirely unknown to all of humanity until that evening.
👑 Herschel wanted to name it **Georgium Sidus** ('George's Star') in honour of King George III of England. The rest of the world politely declined — and the name Uranus eventually prevailed.
🛸 **Voyager 2** is the only spacecraft ever to have flown past Uranus, in **January 1986** — a flyby of a few hours after 9 years of travel. No other probe is currently en route to return.

neptune.name: Neptune
neptune.description:
Neptune is the planet that was **found through mathematics** before anyone had seen it — a bit like guessing someone is in the next room by noticing the furniture moving for no apparent reason. Le Verrier precisely calculated where the culprit disrupting Uranus's orbit must be, and when astronomers in Berlin pointed their telescope at that spot, Neptune was there, **less than one degree from the predicted position**. The planet, indifferent to this triumph of human reason, calmly kept blowing its winds at **2,100 km/h** — the most violent in the solar system. Its moon Triton orbits **backwards**, betraying a gravitational capture from the Kuiper Belt, and is slowly spiralling toward Neptune until its inevitable destruction in **roughly 3.6 billion years**.

> A tragic fate for a moon — but then again, how many of us can claim a guaranteed future at 3 billion years out?
facts: 🌟 **Galileo** had already observed Neptune in **1612** through his own telescope — but mistook it for a fixed star. Had he looked two nights more, he would have detected its movement and rewritten history.
🔄 Since its discovery in **1846**, Neptune has completed just **one full orbit** around the Sun — in 2011. It will pass the same point again in **2175**.

👁️ The **Great Dark Spot** — a storm as wide as Earth observed by Voyager 2 in 1989 — had **vanished** by the time Hubble looked for it in 1994. Neptune recycles its giant storms far faster than Jupiter.

pluto.name: Pluto
pluto.description:
Pluto is **the great misunderstood body of the solar system**: for **76 years** everyone called it a planet, then the IAU changed the rules in 2006 and demoted it. It was a **23-year-old astronomer** armed with a blink comparator who found it in 1930, even though his predecessor Percival Lowell had accidentally photographed it **in 1915 without noticing** — and had been dead for 14 years when Tombaugh made the discovery. Its name was proposed by an **11-year-old schoolgirl** from Oxford who suggested it to her grandfather over breakfast. As for Charon, its giant moon, it is so massive that the system's centre of mass **floats in empty space between the two bodies** — Pluto and Charon dance around a phantom point.

> Its giant heart-shaped surface feature, discovered in 2015, will likely remain the most endearing fact in the entire history of planetary astronomy.
facts: 🐕 Walt Disney named his character **Pluto** in **1930**, the same year as the planet's discovery — whether inspired by it or mere coincidence, the Disney archives do not formally settle the question.
⚛️ The chemical element **plutonium** (no. 94) was named in honour of Pluto in **1941**, following an established tradition: uranium → Uranus, neptunium → Neptune.
📅 In **2178**, Pluto will complete its **first full orbit** since its discovery. Someone born in 1930 would need to live 248 years to celebrate this first 'Plutonian birthday'.

ceres.name: Ceres
ceres.description:
Ceres is **the categorical chameleon of the solar system**: planet in 1801, asteroid in 1852, dwarf planet in 2006 — **three different classifications** in two centuries, an absolute record that nothing and no one can take from it. Discovered on **1 January 1801** by a Sicilian priest who was searching for a star in a catalogue and found something else instead, it was subsequently lost in the Sun's glare — and it was the **24-year-old** mathematician Carl Friedrich Gauss who invented a new orbit-calculation method to recover it, a method still in use today. It contains **roughly one third of all the mass in the asteroid belt** on its own, within an object only 940 km in diameter. Beneath its austere surface, underground brines periodically rise to the surface, evaporate, and leave **bright salt deposits** visible from space.

> Ceres is proof that it is never too late to change professional category.
facts: ⚗️ The chemical element **Cerium** (Ce, no. 58) was named in honour of Ceres in **1803**, just two years after its discovery — at a time when it was still considered a planet.

🛸 The **Dawn** probe is the first to have orbited **two different bodies** in the solar system: it visited asteroid Vesta (2011–2012), then Ceres (2015–2018), before ending its mission there when it ran out of fuel.
🌊 Ceres is estimated to contain more **fresh water** than all of Earth's liquid freshwater reserves combined — locked away as subsurface ice and brines circulating through its mantle.

haumea.name: Haumea
haumea.description:
Haumea is **the dwarf planet that decided to look like nothing else** known: instead of being round like all its peers, it has the shape of a flattened rugby ball — because it rotates on itself in **under 4 hours**, the fastest rotation of any large object in the solar system, and the centrifugal force simply deformed it. Its surface of **nearly pure crystalline water ice** shines like fresh snow in the absolute cold, and since 2017 we have known it even has a **ring** — the first dwarf planet to have one. Its discovery also triggered a scandal: a Spanish team announced the discovery in a rush after, according to the American team, consulting their observation logs without authorisation — the IAU **never designated an official discoverer**.

> It also gave birth to a 'family' of dozens of objects sharing its ice composition — like a fertility goddess who scattered her children to the four corners of the Kuiper Belt.
facts: 🎅 The American team nicknamed it **'Santa'** internally — because they had discovered it on **28 December 2004**, three days after Christmas.

💥 The '**Haumea family**' groups dozens of small TNOs sharing exactly the same water-ice composition — all fragments from the **same ancestral collision** billions of years ago, of which Haumea is the largest remnant.
📅 Haumea will reach its **closest point to the Sun** (perihelion) only in **2133** — it is currently more than 50 AU away, fifty times the Earth-Sun distance.

makemake.name: Makemake
makemake.description:
Makemake is **the dwarf planet that kept its Easter nickname all the way into its official name**: the team that discovered it in 2005 had nicknamed it 'Easterbunny' because they had found it just after Easter — and when the time came to give it a proper name, they deliberately searched for a mythology linked to Easter, and landed on Makemake, the creator god of **Easter Island**. Its rust-coloured surface is covered in frozen methane stained by **tholins** — complex organic compounds formed by cosmic radiation acting on ices. It has a nameless moon, discovered in 2015 by Hubble, so dark it went entirely unnoticed despite orbiting such a bright body. Evidence of **cryovolcanism** and possibly even an underground ocean has been detected.

> For now, Makemake remains a mysterious reddish dot observed from Earth, patiently waiting for its explorer.
facts: 🌑 Makemake's moon, discovered by Hubble in 2015, has an **albedo of roughly 4%** — making it extremely dark, in stark contrast to Makemake itself which reflects **81%** of the light it receives.
📍 Makemake is the **largest object in the classical Kuiper Belt** — a region of stable orbits beyond Neptune, distinct from the scattered disc where the more distant and chaotic Eris resides.
📅 Makemake is currently near its **farthest point from the Sun** (~52.7 AU in 2025) and will not reach its next **perihelion** until **2186** — more than 160 years from now.

eris.name: Eris
eris.description:
Eris is **the dwarf planet that started everything**: when Mike Brown and his team found it in 2005, it appeared larger than Pluto, NASA announced it as the **10th planet**, and world astronomy entered an existential crisis — *forcing the IAU to define for the first time in 2006 exactly what a planet is, a question left without a rigorous answer since Copernicus*. Paradoxically, although it is **27% more massive** than Pluto, it is slightly smaller in size — simply denser, like a more compact cake. Its surface reflects **96% of the light** it receives, making it one of the brightest objects in the solar system — a near-perfect mirror ball lost at **almost 100 times the Earth-Sun distance**.

> Its discoverer had nicknamed it 'Xena' before naming it after the goddess of Discord — *finding that the name perfectly described the trouble it had caused*.
facts: 🌑 Eris's moon is named **Dysnomia** — the Greek goddess of **Lawlessness and Deception**, daughter of Eris in mythology. A thematically impeccable choice.

🕵️ The original images of Eris date from **21 October 2003** — but the analysis software had ignored them because Eris was moving too slowly. It was only identified in **January 2005** during a manual re-analysis.
📖 Mike Brown, its discoverer, is nicknamed **'the Pluto Killer'** — he even wrote a book under that title, fully embracing the scientific and cultural controversy he had set in motion.

welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.description: solarsys is an interactive 3D solar system. Explore planets, moons and orbits in real time.

camera.title: Camera Controls
camera.description: Left-click and drag to orbit. Scroll to zoom in and out. Right-click and drag to pan.

select.title: Select Bodies
select.description: Click on any celestial body to focus the camera on it. Press SPACE to exit focus mode.

menu.title: Menu
menu.description: Click the top-left corner to open the menu. Toggle wireframe, axes and grid helpers for each body.

zoom.title: Zoom Indicator
zoom.description: The top bar shows your current zoom level. Use it to gauge your distance from the scene center.

time.title: Time Control
time.description: Use the time-scale control at the bottom to speed up or slow down the orbital simulation.

lang.title: Language
lang.description: Switch between English and French at any time. The entire interface updates instantly.

tactical.title: Tactical View
tactical.description: Click the bottom-right triangle to toggle the tactical top-down view, giving you a bird's-eye perspective of all orbits.

ready.title: Ready to Explore
ready.description: You're all set! Dive into the solar system and discover its wonders.
